action: Vanderbilt students and staff: follow university instructions before reconnecting devices, change passwords when asked, and watch for phishing that references the incident.
date_note: University says it began defending against the cyberattack on 9 November at about 8:30 a.m.; the entry is updated through the 19 November notice.
exec: A major research university is operating with restricted systems; the group's data-theft claim is unconfirmed.
impact: Most systems and applications were available again by the 19 November update; OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams remained disabled.
plain: Vanderbilt University restricted many computer systems after a cyberattack. A group called BYOD claims it stole details of more than a million people; the university has not confirmed that.
summary: Vanderbilt told students and staff on November 9 to shut down university devices during an active cybersecurity incident, which it calls a cyberattack. Its 19 November update says most systems and applications are available, while OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams stay disabled. The BYOD group claims it took more than 1 million Social Security numbers; the university has not confirmed this. A former student has filed a proposed class action; its allegations are untested.
title: Vanderbilt University restricts systems after cyberattack; BYOD ransomware group claims 1 million records

validation.note: University updates page (6 p.m. Nov. 19), Government Technology and Beinsure read; the university does not use the word ransomware, and the theft claim and lawsuit allegations are unconfirmed.

review.note: Compared with university updates page, GovTech, Beinsure: date moved from 13 Nov to 9 Nov (university start); title and plain no longer state ransomware as fact (university says cyberattack; label from GovTech); more than a million per the claim; SharkStriker tracker removed from sources
